correctness.rationale: Lemma 1 (translation fixing for pairwise-coprime C): proof checked. Pairwise-coprime divisors of L have product dividing L by prime-exponent argument; CRT gives t with a_c+t=0 for all c in C; permutation x->x+t preserves density. Empirically confirmed on [7,8,9,10] (full 5040-combo optimum 1032/2520 equals C-fixed optimum). Lemma 2 (prime peeling): proof checked. Equivalence p prime with no multiples <=> p not dividing L0 holds because p|L0 iff p divides some m in S0. Lift counting uses gcd(L0,p)=1 so y+tL0 runs through all residues mod p; uncovered=(L0-c0)(p-1), D=D0+U0/p independent of a_p. Empirically confirmed on S0=[7,8,9,10] lifted by 11: all 11 residues give 12840/27720=107/231 as predicted. Iteration for distinct new primes valid as removal cannot create multiples. Lemma 3 (prime-max exchange): proof checked with one implicit step made explicit: any 9-set in [7,60] with prime max has max>=17 (7..13 contains only 7 numbers), while smallest unused m* in [7,24] is <=16 (7..16 contains 10 numbers), so m*<m_max; averaging argument Dmax(S')>=D0+U0/m* holds for any divisibility because for fixed S0 pattern each uncovered x is hit by exactly one of m* residues. Hence no optimal set has prime maximum. Union-bound maximizer 7..15 with sum 62575/72072 verified by Fraction; exchange by 1/m monotonicity valid. Witness densities verified by independent stdlib bytearray LCM enumeration: 36340/55440=1817/2772, 3290/5040=47/72, top-5 table rows match. Table completeness verified: 2002 distinct rows equal all C(14,9) subsets of [7,20], sorted descending. Core optima independently re-proved by a different branch-and-bound (union-bound pruning, no affine orbits): best core 3130/5040 (120960 combos brute-forced in 0.9s), runner-up 3290/5040 (2177280 combos in 15.3s), hardest 43M-combo core [8,9,10,12,14,15,16,18,20] proved 3140/5040 in 1.4s with 15783 nodes, 10-core random sample all optimal, and full 2002-set independent B&B in 106.4s found zero cases beating the table. Deterministic replay reproduce_census_7_20.py reran in 27.0s asserting best 1817/2772. Corollary interval for [7,60] follows rigorously from witness (lower) and union bound (upper). Machine-checked enumeration is experimental evidence with two independent implementations agreeing; lemmas are proofs.

originality.rationale: Claim-level comparison across hypotheses, quantifiers, parameter ranges, exact constants, method scope, and conclusion. The candidate's hard core is: exact maximum D*(9;[7,20])=1817/2772 (uncovered 955/2772) attained at S*=[7,8,9,10,11,12,14,15,16] with explicit residues, L=55440, 36340 covered; runner-up 47/72 at [7,8,9,10,12,14,15,16,18] with gap 0.002706; certified interval 0.655483<=D*(9;[7,60])<=0.868229 with union-bound maximizer 7..15 (62575/72072); prime-max exchange lemma; [7,60] equality only conjectured. (1) Hough gives a universal bound on least moduli of full coverings, no fixed-stratum exact maximum. (2) Balister et al. give asymptotic uncovered-density lower bounds and structural theorems, no exact finite census or rational constants. (3) Zhang & Zhang solve LCM-minimality for full coverings with min modulus 7; full-text keyword check (1817, 2772, maximal density, nine moduli, [7,20], [7,60] all absent) confirms a different objective whose density-1 solutions cannot imply a 0.65548 partial-density maximum. (4) Agrawal et al. full text classifies only full coverings with min modulus 2 and prime factors <=5, disjoint from a >=7 partial-density optimum involving 7 and 11. (5) Dalton-Jones and Klein et al. give qualitative interval non-existence and j-th-modulus growth bounds, neither stating nor implying any exact density constant. Exact-formulation arXiv search (maximal+covering+density+moduli) returned 0 total results; minimum-modulus-7 search returned only Zhang; Crossref exact-fraction search returned only unrelated records (thermal insulation, dentistry). No retrieved source states, tabulates, or mathematically implies 1817/2772, 955/2772, the S* witness, the 47/72 runner-up, or the [7,60] certified interval.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a citable Erdős-benchmark number with reusable certificate, not a textbook restatement or parameter tweak. Textbook gives only Mirsky-Newman and 2,3,4,6,12 full covering (density 1, min<=2) and union bound 0.868; exact optimum 0.65548 requires handling overlaps and joint modulus+residue optimization, shown non-trivial by gap 0.002706 to runner-up 47/72 and by composite-beats-prime-heavy phenomenon (best union 0.8538 set is not best true density; 7..15 union 0.868 vs true 0.645). Stratum is principled: [7,60]x9 is first reciprocal-sum-impossible stratum (max sum 0.868<1), and [7,20] closure is the largest exactly closed sub-stratum (2002 sets, 544 cores) with honest limitation that full [7,60] (5.3B sets) remains open; prime-max elimination lemma is general reusable progress. Output is not an unexplained enumeration: divisor-lattice peeling + translation fixing + orbit/B&B method, reduced-fraction CRT replay in <2s, full deterministic replay in 27s, 2002-row table with residues and peel chains. Falls outside rejection classes: not mere substitution (threshold-justified), not tiny unmotivated gain (first exact table for min>=7 k=9), not bare dump (method + proofs + verifiers).
